LESSON: RADIOACTIVITY AND STABILITY OF ISOTOPES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Waves and Optics
Topic 2.2: Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes, part of Waves and Optics in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How is radioactivity important in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Radioactivity and Stability of Isotopes together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: the learner practices how to organize their own learning by learning independently as they construct

a simple leaf electroscope using locally available materials.

• Self-efficacy: the learner develops the skill of effective communication by executing tasks while performing

experiments to verify the uses of an electroscope in electrostatics.

58

Values:
• Respect: the learner shows acceptance as they understand and appreciate others when searching, discussing in groups

and presenting findings on safety precautions when handling radioactive substances.

• Citizenship: the learner shows care by avoiding to hurt others while working with peers to demonstrate the detection

of radioactive emissions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Citizenship education: the learner practices peace and conflict resolution mechanisms as a way of promoting peace

while searching from print materials in appropriate font colour contrast, braille materials or non-print media with

assistive technology on applications of radioactivity.

• Socio-Economic and Environmental issues: the learner demonstrates environmental conservation awareness as they

search, discuss in groups and present findings on safety precautions when handling and disposing radioactive

substances.

51

Suggested learning resources:

digital media with assistive technology such as screen magnifiers, screen readers and adapted keyboard, braille media,

print media in appropriate font and colour contrast , manilla papers, marker pens, braille reading and writing materials,

print graphs, tactile graphs, leaf electroscope, photographic emulsion plate, cloud chamber, GM tube, burette, digital

talking stopwatch,

Suggested key skills;

• illustrate how radionuclides attain their stability using nuclear equations,

• determine the half-life (t1/2) of common radioactive elements,

52
